fatal_errors: The proposed W-Ta-Ti alloy omits V and Zr from the target equimolar WTaTiVZr composition.
It replaces the target arc-melted, repeatedly remelted as-cast alloy and its tungsten comparison with an unspecified solid solution and generic elemental addition.

The asserted irradiation resistance, low neutron-absorption cross-section, irradiation-induced precipitation, and grain-boundary strengthening are not demonstrated for the proposed W-Ta-Ti material by the cited evidence.
The claimed 1000-2000 K boundary does not match the target measurements, which covered room temperature to 500 °C and did not test reactor irradiation or operating fusion conditions.

The falsification rule is scientifically weak because irradiation-induced dislocation accumulation or grain-size changes alone would not necessarily falsify useful irradiation resistance or high-temperature structural performance.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the broad fusion-PFC motivation and names three constituents of the target alloy, but it fails to reconstruct the actual WTaTiVZr material, processing, two-BCC dendritic microstructure, test conditions, strengthening interpretation, or quantitative advantages over coarse-grained powder-sintered tungsten. Its outcome is only directionally similar at a generic level. The cited papers establish broad motivation and irradiation behavior in other HEA systems, not the claimed properties or low activation of W-Ta-Ti. It also extrapolates to an untested reactor-temperature and irradiation regime, whereas the target explicitly limits its conclusions to quasi-static mechanical tests through 500 °C and room-temperature scratch toughness.
